label: OSHA reporting of fatalities, hospitalizations, amputations and eye loss
statusNote: A summary for exercises. Each clock runs from when the employer or its agent learns of the event (or learns it was work-related). A death is reportable when it occurs within 30 days of the incident; an in-patient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye when it occurs within 24 hours of the incident. An in-patient hospitalization is a formal admission for care or treatment, not observation or diagnostic testing alone. Report by telephone or in person to the nearest area office, to 1-800-321-OSHA or with the online form; a message, fax or email does not count. State plans may be stricter: California requires a report within 8 hours for a serious injury or illness as well as a death.

triggers.label: Work-related fatality learned of
triggers.hint: The employer learns that an employee died from a work-related incident.

triggers.label: In-patient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye learned of
triggers.hint: The employer learns of an in-patient hospitalization of one or more employees, an amputation or the loss of an eye from a work-related incident.

clocks.label: Report a work-related fatality
clocks.recipient: OSHA area office, the OSHA 24-hour hotline or the online form
clocks.rule: Report a work-related fatality within 8 hours.

clocks.label: Report an in-patient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye
clocks.recipient: OSHA area office, the OSHA 24-hour hotline or the online form
clocks.rule: Report an in-patient hospitalization, an amputation or the loss of an eye within 24 hours.

appliesTo.note: Employers covered by the OSHA Act, including contractors and subcontractors on construction sites.
